note: SECOND SHAPE for #3872. The issue title says the signature is 'allowed'; the front end and the DXIL validator are separate gates, and 'dxc accepts it but the validator rejects it' would be a materially less severe finding than 'nothing catches it'. This predicate scores the validator arm: it MATCHES when DXIL validation rejected the module. dxc runs validation on every compile in cmd.txt (no -Vd anywhere), and this build ships its own dxil.dll beside dxc.exe, so a clean exit already means validation passed -- but an unfired predicate is unreadable without proof it can fire. POSITIVE CONTROL, captured in this directory: control-valfail.hlsl is the same five-entry-point pipeline with no SV_ShadingRate at all and a deliberately incompatible [RootSignature("DescriptorTable(SRV(t0))")] against a Texture1D at t3; run under the repro's own command lines with --expect match, it must produce 'error: validation errors'. NEGATIVE CONTROL: control-nosr.hlsl under this same predicate with --expect no-match. Together they make a no-match on the repro mean 'the validator ran and passed it', not 'nothing was measured'. The marker text is dxc's own wrapper line for a failed IDxcValidator run (tools/clang/tools/dxclib/dxc.cpp), the same line tools/clang/test/DXILValidation/rootSigDefine10.hlsl checks for.
